newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN urges Italy, Greece to let in Albanian refugees.
newsitem.headline: UN urges Italy, Greece to let in Albanian refugees.

text.p: The United Nations refuge agency has urged Italy and Greece to allow in Albanians fleeing anarchy in their homeland, a spokeswoman said on Friday.

Spokeswoman Make Shinohara also told Reuters the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) was helping the Italian and Greek governments to set up camps for Albanians, but so far there was no significant movement of refugees into either state.
Albania's chaotic revolt, which erupted after thousands lost their savings in bogus investment schemes, has engulfed the south of the country and spread to the north in the past two days.

Shinohara said that the Geneva-based agency was in talks with Italy and Greece over plans to set up camps to hold up to 1,000 and 3,000 respectively. It had no figures for the number of Albanians who have fled abroad by land or sea.

"We are asking these governments not to send Albanians back if they come in for the time being, because it is a conflict situation. We are saying if they do flee, let them in and let them stay as long as necessary under acceptable conditions."
The UNHCR had also been in touch with Yugoslavia, which has closed its border with Albania, and asked it to be "more generous", according to Shinohara.
